correctness.rationale: For all integers a,b>=2, unique source-removal layers alternate and encode orientations bijectively; Hasse covers are precisely consecutive-block complete bipartite links; this graph is a tree iff interior blocks are singleton. The tree edge lattice basis establishes unimodular smooth toric cones. Odd/even labeled-block counting proves the formula; the bivariate EGF follows from exponential-block weights with a,b>=2 truncation. Replayed checker independently recomputed all acyclic transitive reductions in six complete examples. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Counting the smooth zero-dimensional toric strata in graphical fans is intrinsic geometry: total zonotope vertices and global nonsimplicity do not recover the smooth-point subset. The complete parameter-uniform count, EGF and balanced asymptotic are a natural exact invariant of the widely studied complete-bipartite graphical arrangement; the singleton-interior block classification explains the count. The result is not a selected arbitrary finite count or a known total-f-vector recalculation.
